texts: Write a doha about a touchstone that shows true metal only under pressure, as sorrow shows who truly remembers God, since men call on Him in suffering but forget Him in the ease of good times.
touchstone, remember God always
doha about how we only pray when things go wrong, touchstone idea
When my business collapsed I felt tested like metal on a touchstone and started praying every morning, and now that it has recovered I realised last week that I haven't said a word to God in months.
In sorrow the touchstone finds the heart bright with prayer; in joy it finds the same heart dull and forgetful.
I noticed that I only call my mother when I need money or comfort, and when things are good I forget to call for weeks, and it made me think about how I treat God too.
remember Him in comfort
doha about only praying when life is hard and forgetting when it's good
Please write a doha about the human habit of calling on the Lord in suffering and forgetting Him in comfort, and say that if we remembered Him always, in good times too, no suffering would ever come.
In grief all lips whisper His name; in gladness the lips grow dumb. Remember Him in both, O heart.
The night before the exam I prayed hard under the stars and sent a fly out the window with a vow to be devoted forever, yet by the next week I had forgotten all my promises.
stars and fly doha about only remembering God when you're in trouble
Under the stars the sufferer prays; in daylight, like a fly, he buzzes off and forgets.
stars, fly, remember in comfort
Write a doha about a man who prays to the Lord under the stars when in pain and forgets Him when the fly of daily pleasure buzzes around him, and teach him to remember always.
house and sun doha - we remember God in trouble but forget Him when happy
Please write a doha about a man whose house is full of comfort under the bright sun, who forgets God entirely, and who calls out to Him only when sorrow darkens the roof over his head.
house, sun, forgetting God
In the sunlit house of pleasure we forget Him; in the dark of sorrow we cry His name.
When the sun is bright and my house is full of guests, I forget my prayers completely, but the day the power failed and a family illness hit, I was on my knees.
furnace, well, remember always
In the furnace of sorrow all call the Lord; at the well of ease none remember to give thanks.
During the hardest year of my life in the furnace of illness I prayed constantly, and by the well of recovery I stopped, which made me ashamed.
Write a doha about the furnace of suffering in which all remember the Lord and the deep well of comfort at which they forget Him, urging us to remember Him in both.
furnace and well doha about calling on God in trouble but forgetting Him when all is fine
The fly buzzes round the mosque in happy hours; in grief it settles, trembling, at the Lord's feet.
My friend skips the mosque on every happy occasion, but when his father fell ill, the fly-infested hospital corridor saw him praying more fervently than anyone.
fly and mosque doha - people remember God in pain and forget him in joy
fly, mosque, forgetting God
Compose a doha about a man who never visits the mosque in his happy years, though flies of pleasure swarm around him, but runs there in sorrow, and teach him to remember always.
My brother promised God he'd change if the boat he was sailing in survived the storm, and now that he is safe on shore he has already broken every promise.
In the storm, the boat's captain prayed; on the calm sea, he forgot the Lord who calmed it.
boat, storm, forgotten prayer
Please write a doha about a sailor who prays loudly on a sinking boat, vows great vows, and then, once safe in harbour, forgets both vows and the Lord who saved him.
boat doha about people praying only when in danger
remember Him in joy
In sorrow all remember Him, in joy none; if one remembered Him in joy, why would sorrow come at all?
Write a doha for a person who prays only in trouble, reminding him that the Lord should be remembered in both pain and happiness, and that the one who remembers Him in joy will rarely know sorrow.
Looking back at my own life, I see that every time I turned to God was a crisis, and in every calm stretch I did not think of Him once.
doha: people only remember God when suffering, why not remember him when happy
Compose a doha about a traveler who prays on a lonely road in the dark and a physician who forgets the Lord amid his wealth, warning both that remembering God only in trouble is a poor habit.
traveler and physician doha - we only remember God in suffering
traveler, physician, remember always
The traveler prays on the dark road, the physician forgets in his comfortable room; remember Him in the light too.
The physician at our clinic treats dying patients who all beg God for help, and as a fellow traveler through life he admits he forgot Him entirely in his own healthy years.
The philosopher's stone gives treasure, the cuckoo sings in spring; yet the heart remembers God only in winter.
philosopher's stone, cuckoo, forgetting God
When the cuckoo sang in the good season of my life, I forgot all about God; it was only in the winter of my troubles that I looked for a philosopher's stone of faith.
philosopher's stone and cuckoo doha about people only remembering God when in pain
Please write a doha about the cuckoo that sings merrily in the good season and a seeker with a philosopher's stone who forgets the Lord in luck and remembers Him only in sorrow.
In the days of milk and honey no one remembers Him; in the days of famine all lips cry His name.
The baby's milk was running low and I prayed with all my heart that we would manage, and then once the money came through I never thought to say thanks.
milk doha about remembering God only when things are hard
milk, remembering God always
Write a doha about a household that has milk in plenty and forgets the Lord, and that calls on Him only when the milk runs dry and sorrow arrives, and teach them to remember always.
palanquin and cremation ground doha - people remember God only when death or grief comes
Compose a doha about a man who rides in a grand palanquin at his wedding and forgets the Lord, and who stands weeping at the cremation ground for his loved one and calls on Him only then.
At the wedding palanquin no one thinks of Him; at the cremation ground every lip calls out His name.

At my brother's wedding, as he rode in the palanquin, nobody thought of God for a minute, but at the cremation ground where we mourned my uncle two weeks later, everyone prayed as if their lives depended on it.
palanquin, cremation ground, forgetting God
When my tongue was swollen with fever I kept begging God to cure me, and the moment the sandalwood balm worked I went right back to my old careless life.
sandalwood and tongue doha about asking God for help in pain and forgetting Him in comfort
sandalwood, tongue, remember always
Please write a doha about a tongue that calls the Lord's name only when pain makes it cry, and forgets it in the fragrant ease of sandalwood and comfort, and teach it to remember in both states.
In pain the tongue cries out His name; in the scent of sandalwood it falls silent and forgets.
Write a doha about a man who rides high in a palanquin and forgets the Lord, until a snake of misfortune bites him and he calls out to God in pain, and teach him to remember in good times too.
palanquin, snake, forgetting God
My cousin, who showed off in a palanquin at his wedding and never prayed, was bitten by a snake on his honeymoon and has been praying every day since.
In the palanquin of pleasure the Lord is forgotten; when the snake of sorrow bites, the whole heart cries His name.
palanquin and snake doha - we only remember God when something bad happens
The parrot repeats the Name when the master is sad, and goes mute when his forehead mark of success is fresh: so does the heart.
Compose a doha about a parrot that speaks the Lord's name when its owner weeps, and says nothing when he is merry with the forehead mark of success, showing how we forget God in comfort.
parrot, forehead mark, forgetting God
parrot and forehead mark doha about remembering God only in sadness
My uncle wears a big forehead mark and raises a parrot that recites God's name, but he is only devout when ill, and the parrot has learned that too.
The date palm in our yard bears fruit once a year, and my father only prays during the lean months, never during the harvest, which my mother thinks is ungrateful.
In the shade of the date palm of plenty, the heart forgets; in the desert of need it remembers.
Write a doha about a date palm heavy with fruit under which men forget the Lord, and a barren desert where they remember Him, and teach us to keep Him in mind at all times.
date palm doha - we only call out to God when things are hard
date palm, remembering in plenty
winnowing fan, remember Him
winnowing fan doha about forgetting God in good times
Please write a doha about a winnowing fan that separates grain from chaff, and say that the wise man separates sorrow from pleasure, remembering the Lord in both and forgetting Him in neither.
My grandmother winnows grain with her winnowing fan every season, thanking God during the harvest and begging Him during the famine, and she says most people only do the second part.
The winnowing fan beats in the harvest of plenty, and none remember; in the famine of need, all pray.
After the mountain trek went wrong and we were stuck in the cold, my friend prayed all night, but once we were rescued and at the hotel he did not say a word of thanks.
mountain doha about people only turning to God in danger and forgetting Him afterward
Compose a doha about a man stranded on a mountain in a storm who prays with his whole heart, and then forgets the Lord entirely as soon as he is back in comfort, and teach him to remember always.
On the mountain's icy ledge he calls the Lord; in the warm valley he forgets His name.
mountain, forgetting God
Every time I am in trouble I make deals with God, and every time I am comfortable I conveniently forget Him, and I realised recently that this makes me a fair-weather friend.
In sorrow, the Lord is a refuge; in comfort, a stranger. Remember Him in both, and know no sorrow.
short doha about how we only pray in hard times
Write a doha for a person who prays fervently in suffering and forgets the Lord when life is easy, urging him to remember God in both pain and pleasure, since only then will suffering lose its sting.
pain, pleasure, remember Him
Our cook used to pray for rain every day during the drought, and the first day it rained, I saw him laughing and he did not mention God for the rest of the season, and a crow stole his lunch.
Please write a doha about a crow that comes begging in famine and flies away unthankful when it is fed, as men call on the Lord in sorrow and forget Him once they are comfortable.
The crow comes to the courtyard in hunger and forgets the hand that fed it; so does the heart forget.
crow, ungrateful heart
crow doha about people remembering God only when in need
Looking at the way I have lived, I suddenly noticed that my prayers have always been about asking for relief and never once about simply thanking God for good days.
If in joy you remembered Him as you do in grief, no grief would ever come near you.
I would like a doha about how people cry out to the Lord in their pain but forget Him in their joy, and how the one who remembers Him in every state is never troubled by sorrow at all.
sorrow remembers, joy forgets
doha: remember God in good times too, not only in trouble
Write a doha about a man who is rich and happy in his big house, forgetting God entirely, and who cries out to the Lord only when sorrow strikes, and teach him to remember always.
In the great house of ease, the Lord is a guest long forgotten; in the hut of grief, He is a friend remembered.
Whenever my father's house was full of guests and celebration, he never mentioned God, but the night the family faced a crisis he began chanting without stopping.
house, remembered in sorrow
house doha - we only remember God when it's too late or we're hurting
I want a doha about the way people cry to the Lord in times of suffering but forget Him in the good times, and about the wisdom of remembering Him in both, so that no suffering ever has to come.
Sorrow teaches the knees to bend; comfort teaches them to forget. Keep them bent, O heart.
forgetting God in comfort
I noticed this month that I pray constantly when I am worried and not at all on the good days, and I felt embarrassed that I treat God like an emergency number.
doha about people only praying in hard times and forgetting in good times
cage and moneylender doha - people only remember God when trapped or in debt
When the moneylender trapped my uncle in debt like a bird in a cage, he turned to prayer for the first time in years, but forgot God again when he got out.
Caged in debt, the heart cries to the Lord; freed by wealth, it forgets who freed it.
Compose a doha about a man caged by a moneylender's debts who cries to the Lord in despair, and who forgets Him entirely when the debt is cleared and comfort returns.
cage, moneylender, forgot God
fire, ash, remember always
In the fire of pain all call upon the Lord; in the ash of comfort, none remember the flame.
fire and ash doha about calling God in trouble and forgetting in good times
Please write a doha about the fire of suffering that makes people cry out to the Lord, and the cool ash of comfort in which they forget Him, and urge them to remember Him always.
After the fire damaged our shop, my father prayed all night, but once everything was rebuilt and only ash remained of the memory, he stopped completely.
doha about how we remember God in pain but not in comfort
Compose a doha for a person who spends joyful days in forgetfulness and sorrowful days in prayer, teaching that to remember the Lord in both is the only wise way to live.
pain remembers, joy forgets
When suffering knocks, we kneel; when pleasure comes, we rise and forget why we knelt.
It struck me at my friend's funeral that when life is easy, none of us even think about what matters, and we only wake up when something terrible happens.
Write a doha about a bridge that people cross in prayer when sorrow comes and burn behind them when comfort returns, forgetting the Lord who carried them over.
bridge, ungrateful memory
When I crossed the old bridge into the hospital to see my sick mother I prayed with all my heart, but on the way out after her recovery I did not give thanks once.
We cross the bridge of sorrow in prayer, and burn it once we reach the shore of comfort.
bridge doha about forgetting God after he helps you
Please write a doha about a fly that lands on honey and forgets everything else, as men in comfort forget the Lord, only to remember Him when they are stuck and struggling.
During a calm and happy year, I became so caught up in my pleasures like a fly in honey that I forgot to pray at all, until a shock reminded me.
fly, honey, forgetting God
fly doha - we forget God in comfort and call him in trouble
The fly sits on the honey of pleasure and is stuck; then it cries to the Lord in pain.
Compose a doha about how the Lord is forgotten in the days of ease and remembered in the days of pain, and about the truth that those who keep Him in mind through both will be spared much suffering.
Pain makes a prayer of the lips; pleasure makes a stranger of the Lord.
When I was fired I turned to God and when I was hired again I forgot Him within a week, and I only noticed this pattern yesterday while sitting in the garden.
doha about remembering God in both joy and sorrow
sorrow prays, joy forgets
cloth sheet, salt, remember always
cloth sheet and salt doha about crying to God in suffering and forgetting him in comfort
Wrapped in a cloth sheet of sorrow, the heart tastes salt tears and calls on the Lord; in ease it forgets.
Write a doha about a person wrapped in a cloth sheet of sorrow, whose tears taste of salt as he calls on the Lord, and who forgets Him once comfort returns, and teach him to remember always.
During the weeks of my mother's illness I wept into a cloth sheet and prayed constantly, but once she recovered and life resumed its salt and spice, I forgot all about God.
On the days when things go badly I find myself praying for hours, and on days when everything goes smoothly I do not give God one thought, and it feels hypocritical.
Only in pain do we call upon Him; in pleasure the Lord is left waiting at the gate of memory.
I would like a doha that says the Lord should be remembered in joy as much as in suffering, and that most people only turn to Him when misfortune strikes, which is why misfortune keeps coming.
remember Him in joy
short doha about only praying in hard times
Last week at the hospital I begged God for my father's recovery, but I noticed during the good times that I had hardly spoken to Him at all, and I felt ashamed.
Write a doha about a man who prays to the Lord only in the days of misfortune and neglects Him in the days of fortune, and teach him to keep God in his heart through both.
forgetting God in good times
doha about the shame of only praying when you need something from God
In sorrow I called Him Father; in joy I forgot His name. Forgive me, Lord, and keep me mindful.
The moon forgets the darkness when it shines, and men forget the Lord in the brightness of luck.
On a bright moonlit night after my promotion, my wife reminded me that I had stopped praying; I had begged God daily during my unemployment.
moon doha about forgetting God when things are good
Compose a doha about the moon that shines in the night sky and forgets its dark side, as men in the brightness of fortune forget the Lord they cried to in the darkness of sorrow.
moon, forgetting God
musk deer, forgetting God
musk deer doha about only remembering God when suffering
The musk deer runs frantic in pain; in ease, it forgets the scent of the Lord inside it.
Please write a doha about a musk deer that races through the woods in terror, calling on the Lord, and forgets Him the moment the danger passes and ease returns.
My neighbour was terrified when his musk deer-skin rug was stolen and turned to prayer, but once it was returned he went back to ignoring God.
Write a doha for the person who has had comfort for a long time and forgotten to pray, warning him that suffering is the Lord's reminder to those who remember Him only in pain.
I've been so busy and comfortable lately that I stopped my daily prayer, and my wife said that it takes a crisis to remind me, and she's right.
remember Him daily
doha about remembering God every day, not only when something goes wrong
If you forget Him in comfort, sorrow comes to remind you; remember Him now and spare yourself.
joy forgets, grief remembers
When I was at my lowest I prayed every hour, and now that I am comfortable I find my mind full of everything but God, and it bothers me.
Compose a doha about how people in great suffering turn to the Lord and in great happiness turn away from Him, and how a wise person keeps Him in mind at all times, equal in joy and in pain.
doha about how happiness makes us forget God
Happiness is the wine that makes the heart forget; sorrow is the sobering that brings it back to the Lord.
The cuckoo sings in the spring of plenty; in the autumn of need, it cries out to the Lord.
My cuckoo-loving grandmother says everyone is a singer in good times and a supplicant in bad, and the same goes for how we speak to God.
cuckoo doha - we remember God in hard times but forget in good
cuckoo, forgetting God
Write a doha about a cuckoo that sings in spring and goes silent in autumn, as people sing God's praises in sorrow but forget Him in the spring of their good fortune.
At the crossroads the thief calls on the Lord in fear; once he is safe, he returns to his thieving ways.
A thief who was caught at the crossroads in our town swore before God that he would reform, and was seen back at his old business a week after he was released.
thief, crossroads, forgot God
Please write a doha about a thief at a crossroads who prays loudly to the Lord when the crowd closes in, and forgets Him the moment he escapes, as men forget God when their trouble passes.
thief and crossroads doha about people remembering God only in danger
tortoise, forgetting God
Write a doha about a tortoise that pulls into its shell when danger comes and forgets everything else once safe, as men turn to the Lord in danger and forget Him in the ease that follows.
The tortoise draws in its limbs at danger, and in safety forgets the shelter; so does the heart forget the Lord.
My pet tortoise hides in its shell the moment I come near and wanders around carelessly the rest of the day, and it reminded me of how I treat prayer.
tortoise doha about running to God in trouble and ignoring Him otherwise
The sword is drawn and the net is cast; in fear we pray, in safety we forget.
Compose a doha about a man hunted by enemies with sword and net, who prays loudly to the Lord for deliverance and forgets Him entirely once he has escaped.
When the robbers came into the village with swords and nets for the cattle, everyone prayed together, but the next morning, safe and sound, nobody thought of God again.
sword and net doha - people only call on God when in danger
sword, net, forgetting God
When my daughter was hospitalised I prayed every minute, and now that she is back at school I realised that my prayers had quietly stopped, and felt a pang about it.
doha about remembering God when life is good, not just when it's bad
Be as devoted in sunshine as in the storm, O heart; the Lord is the same in both.
Write a doha reminding people that God is the same in pain and in pleasure, and that the wise person remembers Him in both, not just when suffering comes calling.
remember God always
The peacock dances in the season of joy, the traveler prays in the night of fear; remember Him in both.
peacock and traveler doha about forgetting God when happy and praying when scared
peacock, traveler, forgetting God
On a long trip as a traveler, I prayed nonstop through a scary night, but at the peacock-filled resort the next day I did not think of God once.
Write a doha about a peacock dancing in the pride of comfort, forgetting the Lord, and a traveler who prays desperately on a dark road, teaching both to remember Him always, in joy and in sorrow.
rainbird, oil press, remember Him
Please write a doha about a rainbird that cries for rain in the dry months and forgets it in the wet, and an oil press that groans under load, showing men call on the Lord only in hardship.
The rainbird cries in drought and sleeps in rain; the oil press groans in pain: so we call on Him only in distress.
rainbird and oil press doha - we only call God when it's hard
During the drought my uncle at the oil press prayed daily for rain with the rainbird calling outside, but when the rains came he stopped the prayers entirely.
remember Him, joy and sorrow
My mother says the difference between the devout and the rest is that the devout keep the same prayer on their lips on good days and bad.
Equal in gain and loss, equal in song and tears, the lover keeps the Lord in mind.
Compose a doha for the person who prays fervently in suffering and forgets in pleasure, advising him to hold the Lord in his heart equally in joy and sorrow, and be free of both.
doha: remember God the same in good times and bad
fish doha about only turning to God when in trouble
The fish flops on dry land and cries to the Lord; back in water, it forgets Him entirely.
Write a doha about a fish thrown on dry land that cries to the Lord for help and, back in the water, swims on without a thought of Him, as men do when trouble passes.
My uncle fishes for a living and says that every fish he lands thrashes in panic, but you can bet they forget the fear the moment they are back in water, like people with prayer.
fish, forgetting God
thread doha - people pray when the thread of life is about to snap, then forget
thread, remember Him always
Compose a doha about the fragile thread of life that makes men pray when it is about to snap, and about how they forget the Lord as soon as it holds firm again.
When my father was on a ventilator and life hung by a thread, I prayed day and night, but when he came home I slipped right back into forgetting God.
When the thread of life is thin we pray; when it is strong we forget the One who spun it.
dew, tree, remember Him
Write a doha about dew on the leaves of a great tree that shines in the good hours and vanishes at noon, as man's remembrance of God vanishes in the ease of good days.
Under the old tree where my father prayed fervently through his illness, dew was glistening on the grass, and I realised he never prayed there again once he recovered.
The dew glitters on the tree in the morning of joy and is gone by noon; so is our remembrance.
dew and tree doha about remembering God only in hard times
I want a doha that says suffering is a gift because it reminds us of God, but happiness makes us forget Him, so the wise person keeps remembrance alive in both and is never lost.
After a lifetime I have learned that my best prayers have all come in my worst hours, and that in my best hours I am the farthest from God.
doha about how suffering makes us remember God and happiness makes us forget
pain brings prayer
Sorrow is the Lord's reminder to a heart grown careless in joy.
Please write a doha about a man wrapped in a cloth sheet in the cold of misfortune who cries out to the Lord, but who forgets Him in the warmth of comfort, and teach him to remember always.
Sleeping on the street under a cloth sheet in the cold, a man told me he prayed every night, but said he never prayed when he lived in comfort years before.
cloth sheet doha about praying in hardship and forgetting in comfort
cloth sheet, remember always
In the thin cloth sheet of misery the Lord is remembered; in the silk of comfort He is lost.
A diamond is prized in joy and pawned in pain; so the Lord is forgotten in joy and cried to in pain.
diamond, forgetting God
Compose a doha about a diamond worn proudly in the good days and sold in the hard ones, as the Lord is forgotten in comfort and remembered only when sorrow strips a man of everything.
My aunt wore her diamond to every party and never prayed, then sold it to pay for my uncle's surgery and has prayed daily since, which my cousin finds a little ironic.
diamond doha about remembering God only when things go wrong
